==Problem==
If <math>20\%</math> of a number is <math>12</math>, what is <math>30\%</math> of the same number? 

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 15\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 18\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 20\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 24\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 30 </math>

==Solution==
<math>20\%</math> of a number is equal to <math>\frac{1}{5}</math> of that number. Let <math>n</math>=the number

<math>\frac{1}{5}n = 12</math> Multiply both sides by 5

<math>n = 60</math>

<math>30\%</math> of <math>n</math> is equal to <math>\frac{3}{10}n = \frac{3}{10}\cdot60 = 3\cdot6 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}18}</math>
